The socioeconomic benefits will be achieved through efforts to protect the gardens and fields of households frequently raided by problem animals with electric fencing and block farming. Concurrently, the project will work with District Local Governments to support sustainable land management and climate smart agriculture to ensure the farms are not just safe from wildlife raids, but that farm resilience and productivity is increased. The target communities that will directly benefit from the project are drawn from 42 sub-counties in the seven project districts Table 6. Distribution of project beneficiaries by district and sub-county Sub-region Districts Sub-counties No. of beneficiaries/ District Males Females Karamoja sub-region Karenga Kapedo, Kawalakor, Sangar, Lobalangit, Lokori, Napore-Karenga, Karenga Town Council 7,164 7,456 Kaabong Kalapata, Lolelia, Lodiko, Kathile, Sidok, Kamion, Loyoro 13,171 13,709 Kotido Kacheri, Panyangara, Rengen, Kotido, Kotido Town Council 21,531 22,409 Abim Alerek, Njakwae, Morulem, Owamige, Lotuke, Abim Town Council. 17,914 18,646 Acholi sub-region Agago Omuya-Pacwa, Paimol, Lapono, Adilang, Lokule, Kalongo, Arum, Lira-Palwo 12,863 13,388 Kitgum Mucwini, Oromo, Namakora, Omiya Anyima 11,412 11,878 Lamwo Agoro, Madi Opei, Lokung, Paloga 7,257 7,553 Total 91,312 95,039 The project will generate socio economic benefits through: · Supporting conservation of 114,000 ha of buffer areas (i.e. wildlife reserves, forest reserves) in the Kidepo landscape to increase wildlife foraging areas and reduce the pressure on farmlands. · Establishment of 14,000 ha of pilot block and electric fencing for farmers to reduce damage from problem animal raids, and support for value addition for conservation friendly agriculture including for oil seeds, and other crops that do not attract problem animals. Improved crop production and value addition is expected to benefit women in their gender role as providers in the sub-regions where female headed households far exceed male headed households. · Support sustainable land planning and climate smart agriculture for 35,000 ha of farmland, including agro forestry to provide biomass energy particularly for female headed households and youth. The project will explore establishment of a carbon credits market for the 3,153,457 MtCO2e. The carbon credits generated will create a new revenue stream. · Low skilled employment opportunities for community members who will be engaged in the removal of invasive species and rehabilitation of watering points in the KVNP and KCWA. The project will target boosting income for women for youth. · Employment and enterprise development for establishment of wildlife-based enterprises will be developed through scaling up public-private partnerships with Uganda Wildlife Safaris (UWS), Karatunga, and other operators.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
